title: They Feared God More Than a King: The Night Two Midwives Defied an Empire
paragraphs: They Feared God More Than a King: The Night Two Midwives Defied an Empire
When death was commanded and silence was safer, two unnamed women chose obedience to God—and history has never been the same.

There are moments in life when fear feels logical… when silence feels wise… when going along with what’s wrong feels safer than standing for what’s right. And then there are moments like this—when heaven watches closely, when eternity leans in, when two ordinary women step into a decision that would echo through generations.
Their names were Shiphrah and Puah.
Not queens. Not warriors. Not prophets standing on mountains.
Midwives.
Hands that caught life before it ever took its first breath.
And Pharaoh—king of Egypt, ruler of power, feared by nations—gave them a command that still chills the soul.
“Kill the sons.”
The order is preserved in the Hebrew text of Exodus 1:16, and its weight doesn’t soften with time:

“בְּיַלֶּדְכֶן אֶת־הָעִבְרִיּוֹת וּרְאִיתֶן עַל־הָאָבְנָיִם אִם־בֵּן הוּא וַהֲמִתֶּן אֹתוֹ וְאִם־בַּת הִוא וָחָיָה”
“When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women and see them upon the birthstool, if it is a son, you shall put him to death, but if it is a daughter, she shall live.”
No courtroom. No appeal. No mercy.
Just quiet, hidden murder.
And here is where everything changes.
Because Scripture does not say they hesitated.
It says something far more dangerous.

“וַתִּירֶאןָ הַמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים”
“But the midwives feared God…” (Exodus 1:17)
Not Pharaoh.
Not consequences.
Not loss.
They feared God.
That word “feared” — yare’ — is not trembling terror. It is reverence so deep it rearranges your decisions. It is the kind of fear that makes disobedience to God feel heavier than death itself.
They stood between a king’s command and God’s will…
…and they chose God.
No announcement. No protest. No public rebellion.
Just quiet, unwavering obedience.
They let the boys live.
And in that hidden place, where no one would have known if they obeyed Pharaoh, heaven recorded their names.
Do you feel that?
They didn’t need an audience to obey God.
They didn’t need applause to do what was right.
They didn’t wait until it was safe.
They chose obedience when it cost something.
And here’s the part that exposes us a little…
How many times have we stayed silent because speaking truth felt risky?
How many times have we justified compromise because “it’s just easier”?
How many times have we feared people more than God?
Be honest.
This isn’t about ancient Egypt anymore.
This is about us.
Because every day we are given quieter versions of Pharaoh’s command…
Stay silent about your faith.
Don’t speak truth—it might offend.
Blend in. Compromise. Keep it comfortable.
And every day, we are given the same choice Shiphrah and Puah faced.
Fear God… or fear everything else.
Their courage didn’t just save lives.
It positioned them inside God’s unfolding redemption story.
Because one of those spared Hebrew boys would one day be placed in a basket…
float down a river…
and grow up to become Moses.
And Moses would confront Pharaoh.
And Moses would lead Israel out of slavery.
And centuries later, through that same lineage, Jesus Christ would step into history.
Do you see it?
Two midwives.
One decision.
And a ripple that leads to the cross.
This is how God works.
He writes eternity through hidden obedience.
He builds redemption through quiet courage.
He rewrites scandal into grace.
And maybe… just maybe… you’ve been underestimating your own obedience.
Maybe you thought your choices didn’t matter.
Maybe you thought your quiet stand wouldn’t change anything.
But heaven sees differently.
God is still writing stories like this.
Through people like you.
Right now.
And listen closely—because this part might hit deeper than you expected—
Shiphrah and Puah were not fearless.
They were just more afraid of dishonouring God than facing consequences.
That’s the difference.
That’s the line.
That’s the kind of faith that changes everything.
And maybe today…
God is asking you the same question without saying a word:
Who do you really fear?
Because your answer is already shaping your life.
Let it confront you.
Let it search you.
Let it change you.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
And someone you know needs this exact moment of truth.
Save this so when fear creeps back in, you remember what obedience looks like.
Because discipleship isn’t a one-time moment.
It’s a daily surrender.
This is more than content.
This is calling.
And if you feel it… don’t ignore it.
Because someone has to stand when it’s not easy.
Someone has to obey when it’s not safe.
Someone has to fear God more than the world.
Why not you?
Because in the quiet places where no one sees, your obedience is already rewriting eternity.
